# Parameter Foundry (Jenkins plugin)

> Jenkins plugin that provides one parameter model for choices and typed input
> across the UI, Pipeline, REST, CLI, Rebuild, and downstream builds. Values are
> canonical, providers are governed, and the core never executes Job-supplied
> code.

Repository: https://github.com/xykong/parameter-foundry-plugin
Plugin short name: `parameter-foundry`
Current symbols: `foundryChoice`, `foundryForm`, `foundryBase64File`, `foundryStashedFile`, `withFoundryFileParameter`

## Core concepts

- `foundryChoice` with `selectionMode: single` returns a string or `null`.
- `foundryChoice` with `selectionMode: multiple` returns an unordered list sorted by machine value.
- `renderer: table` makes the matrix cells the selectable values; missing cells are unavailable and
  disabled cells stay unselectable.
- `foundryForm` returns a typed map or JSON object built from its field schema.
- Options come from inline `choices` or from a Provider referenced by `providerId`; `dependsOn`
  makes the parameter reactive.
- Providers resolve through Connection Profiles that declare base URL, credentials, path and query
  allow-lists, timeouts, and response size bounds.
- Provider types: `foundryStaticProvider`, `foundryManagedConfigProvider`, `foundryRestProvider`,
  `foundryGitRefProvider`, `foundryScriptProvider` (reviewed companion engine), and
  `foundryMappingProvider` for a dependency value → option list mapping with a default list; the
  mapping executes nothing.
- Environment export: `string` or `none` for single selection, `delimited`, `json`, or `none` for
  multiple selection, `json` or `none` plus per-field variables for forms.
- Typed API: `…/parameter-foundry/api/v1/{schema,resolve,validate,build,providers/health,import/preview}`.
- Errors carry stable codes such as `PARAMETER_FOUNDRY_UNKNOWN_VALUE`.
- Migration CLI: `parameter-foundry-migration` scans the controller, previews a
  Job with its decisions and exact diff, and applies one atomic batch per Job;
  `parameter-foundry-migration-verify` stores the before/after A/B evidence on
  the migration record.
- A parameter that the Job's Pipeline declares is reported as blocked: the
  Jenkinsfile has to change, because Declarative re-applies the declared
  parameters at every build and would revert a configuration migration.
- Read-only replacement simulation: `…/parameter-foundry-replacement-simulation/report`
  compares every production Job's recorded values and environment exports with
  the simulated foundry control and reports `EQUIVALENT`, `MISMATCH`,
  `NEEDS_PROVIDER`, `MANUAL_REDESIGN`, `UNVERIFIED`, or `BLOCKED` per parameter.
- The migration page, the retirement dashboard, and every adapter reason,
  decision, fact, and verification case ship in English, Chinese, Japanese, and
  Korean.

## Conventions for generated content

- Prefer Provider-backed parameters over copied option lists.
- Keep machine values stable; change labels, not values.
- Use `defaultMode: none` unless a default is genuinely safe.
- Validate via `api/v1/validate` before scheduling when building tooling.

## Boundaries

- The core plugin never executes Job-supplied Groovy, JavaScript, HTML, or reads controller file
  paths. Scripting and custom rendering live behind reviewed companion contracts.
- Foundry file parameters ship in the single HPI without File Parameters dependencies.
  Base64 is limited to 1 MiB decoded bytes, Stashed File to 100 MiB.
  UI/REST multipart and CLI share bounded ingestion. Typed JSON rejects binary definitions.
  Source file migrations are class B; wrappers change to withFoundryFileParameter,
  ordinary unstash keeps its name, and binary lifecycle needs manual verification.
  Keep source plugins until historical and generated references are retired.
